title: Stalks of a change of rings of a sheaf of modules
statement:
Let $X$ be a topological space, $\varphi:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O'$ a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings on $X$, and $\mathcal F$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules, with change of rings $\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] (the sheafification of $U\mapsto\mathcal F(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O(U)}\mathcal O'(U)$, a sheaf of $\mathcal O'$-modules); for an open $U$, $s\in\mathcal F(U)$ and $a\in\mathcal O'(U)$ write $s\otimes a\in(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O')(U)$ for the image of $s\otimes a$ under the sheafification map. Let $x\in X$; the stalk $\mathcal F_x$ is an $\mathcal O_x$-module and $\mathcal O'_x$ an $\mathcal O_x$-algebra via $\varphi_x$. Then there is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O'_x$-modules
$$\mathcal F_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_x}\mathcal O'_x\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O')_x,$$
natural in $\mathcal F$, sending $s_x\otimes a_x$ to $(s\otimes a)_x$ for every open $U\ni x$, $s\in\mathcal F(U)$, $a\in\mathcal O'(U)$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma Tag 008B (label lemma-stalk-tensor-sheaf-modules), proved from Lemma Tag 007K (lemma-stalk-tensor-presheaf-modules, the presheaf version, proof omitted: stalks are filtered colimits and tensor products commute with filtered colimits) and the fact that stalks commute with sheafification (lemma-stalk-sheafification)

proof.text: *Setting and stalks.* Let $x\in X$ and let $I_x$ be the directed set of open neighbourhoods of $x$ (reverse inclusion). By [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] the stalks $\mathcal O_x$, $\mathcal O'_x$ are rings with germ maps $r\mapsto r_x$, every presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules (resp. $\mathcal O'$-modules) $\mathcal Q$ has an $\mathcal O_x$-module (resp. $\mathcal O'_x$-module) stalk $\mathcal Q_x=\varinjlim_{U\in I_x}\mathcal Q(U)$ with $(rq)_x=r_xq_x$, every element of a stalk is a germ, and a linear morphism $u$ induces the linear map $u_x:q_x\mapsto u(q)_x$. Regarding $\mathcal O'$ as a presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules via $\varphi$ ($r\cdot b=\varphi_U(r)b$), $\varphi$ is $\mathcal O$-linear, so $\varphi_x:\mathcal O_x\to\mathcal O'_x$, $r_x\mapsto\varphi_U(r)_x$, is well defined; it is a ring homomorphism (sums and products of germs are computed on representatives over a common neighbourhood, and $\varphi_U$ is a ring map), and it makes $\mathcal O'_x$ an $\mathcal O_x$-algebra with $r_x\,b_x=(\varphi_U(r)b)_x$. The *presheaf* change of rings $\mathcal P=\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$, $\mathcal P(U)=\mathcal F(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O(U)}\mathcal O'(U)$ with restrictions $s\otimes a\mapsto s|_V\otimes a|_V$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product; Stacks Sheaves, Section section-presheaves-modules], is a presheaf of $\mathcal O'$-modules by $b\cdot(s\otimes a)=s\otimes ba$ on the right factor (restrictions are semilinear since those of $\mathcal O'$ are ring maps), and $\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'=\mathcal P^\#$ is its sheafification as a presheaf of $\mathcal O'$-modules, with sheafification map $\theta:\mathcal P\to\mathcal P^\#$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. So $\mathcal P_x$ and $(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O')_x$ are $\mathcal O'_x$-modules, and $\mathcal F_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_x}\mathcal O'_x$ is an $\mathcal O'_x$-module through the right factor.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 007J (lemma-stalk-module, proof omitted), Section section-presheaves-modules (the tensor product presheaf), Section section-sheafification-presheaves-modules and the definition of the change of rings before Lemma 008B

proof.text: *Sheafification does not change the stalk.* By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] (for the sheaf of rings $\mathcal O'$) the underlying sheaf of abelian groups of $\mathcal P^\#$ is the sheafification of $\mathcal P$ as a presheaf of abelian groups, with unit $\theta$, and $\theta$ is $\mathcal O'$-linear. By [lem-weil-pbc-stalk-sheafification-space] the map $\theta_x:\mathcal P_x\to(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O')_x$, $p_x\mapsto\theta_U(p)_x$, is an isomorphism of abelian groups. It is $\mathcal O'_x$-linear: for $c\in\mathcal O'_x$, $\xi\in\mathcal P_x$ write $c=b_x$, $\xi=p_x$ over a common $U\in I_x$ ($I_x$ directed); then $\theta_x(c\xi)=\theta_U(bp)_x=(b\,\theta_U(p))_x=b_x\,\theta_U(p)_x=c\,\theta_x(\xi)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. So $\theta_x$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O'_x$-modules.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 008B (lemma-stalk-tensor-sheaf-modules), proof: 'the fact that taking stalks commutes with sheafification' (Lemma 007Z, lemma-stalk-sheafification, for the underlying presheaf of sets/abelian groups)

proof.text: *The stalk of the presheaf change of rings (Lemma 007K).* By definition $\mathcal P_x=\varinjlim_{U\in I_x}\mathcal F(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O(U)}\mathcal O'(U)$ with transition maps $s\otimes a\mapsto s|_V\otimes a|_V$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-tensor-varying-rings] to the directed set $I_x$ and the systems $A_U=\mathcal O(U)$ (commutative rings), $M_U=\mathcal F(U)$ and $N_U=\mathcal O'(U)$, the latter an $\mathcal O(U)$-module via $\varphi_U$, all with the restriction maps; these are semilinear over the restrictions of $\mathcal O$ ($\mathcal F$ is an $\mathcal O$-module, and $(\varphi_U(r)a)|_V=\varphi_V(r|_V)a|_V$ since $\varphi$ commutes with restriction and the restrictions of $\mathcal O'$ are ring maps). Here $A=\mathcal O_x$, $M=\mathcal F_x$, $N=\mathcal O'_x$, the coprojections are the germ maps, the $A$-module structure on $M$ is that of [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] and that on $N$ is $r_x b_x=(\varphi_U(r)b)_x$, i.e. the one given by $\varphi_x$ (step 1); $T=\mathcal P_x$. The lemma gives an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_x$-modules $\psi:\mathcal P_x\to\mathcal F_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_x}\mathcal O'_x$ with $\psi((s\otimes a)_x)=s_x\otimes a_x$ for $U\in I_x$, $s\in\mathcal F(U)$, $a\in\mathcal O'(U)$. It is moreover $\mathcal O'_x$-linear: the elements $(s\otimes a)_x$ generate $\mathcal P_x$ as an abelian group (every element is a germ $p_x$ with $p=\sum_k s_k\otimes a_k$), and for $b\in\mathcal O'(U')$, shrinking to a common neighbourhood, $\psi(b_x(s\otimes a)_x)=\psi((s\otimes ba)_x)=s_x\otimes b_xa_x=b_x\,\psi((s\otimes a)_x)$; both sides being additive in the element of $\mathcal P_x$, $\psi(c\xi)=c\psi(\xi)$ for all $c\in\mathcal O'_x$, $\xi\in\mathcal P_x$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 007K (lemma-stalk-tensor-presheaf-modules, proof omitted: written out here; stalks are filtered colimits and tensor products commute with filtered colimits)

proof.text: *The isomorphism and the germs of $s\otimes a$.* Put $\Psi=\theta_x\circ\psi^{-1}:\mathcal F_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_x}\mathcal O'_x\to(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O')_x$, an isomorphism of $\mathcal O'_x$-modules by steps 2 and 3. For $U\ni x$, $s\in\mathcal F(U)$, $a\in\mathcal O'(U)$ the section $s\otimes a$ of the statement is $\theta_U(s\otimes a)$, so $\Psi(s_x\otimes a_x)=\theta_x((s\otimes a)_x)=\theta_U(s\otimes a)_x=(s\otimes a)_x$. The elements $s_x\otimes a_x$ generate $\mathcal F_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_x}\mathcal O'_x$ as an abelian group (every element of $\mathcal F_x$, $\mathcal O'_x$ is a germ, and two germs have representatives over a common neighbourhood), so $\Psi$ is determined by this formula.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 008B (lemma-stalk-tensor-sheaf-modules): the identification is the composite of those of Lemma 007K and Lemma 007Z

proof.text: *Naturality in $\mathcal F$.* Let $u:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F_1$ be a morphism of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules. The morphism $u\otimes1:\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'\to\mathcal F_1\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$ is the sheafification of the morphism of presheaves of $\mathcal O'$-modules $u\otimes_p1:\mathcal P\to\mathcal P_1$, $s\otimes a\mapsto u(s)\otimes a$, i.e. the unique $\mathcal O'$-linear map with $(u\otimes1)\circ\theta=\theta_1\circ(u\otimes_p1)$ [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; hence $(u\otimes1)(s\otimes a)=u(s)\otimes a$ on sections. The additive maps $(u\otimes1)_x\circ\Psi$ and $\Psi_1\circ(u_x\otimes1)$ from $\mathcal F_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_x}\mathcal O'_x$ to $(\mathcal F_1\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O')_x$ both send $s_x\otimes a_x$ to $(u(s)\otimes a)_x$ (step 4 and $u_x(s_x)=u(s)_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]); these elements generate (step 4), so the maps are equal: $\Psi$ is natural in $\mathcal F$.
